3.4a — Turret Damage, Tuning & Playtest

Your turret detects you, aims, and shoots on a timer. But currently, bullets fly harmlessly through your body. Today, you complete the loop by connecting projectile impacts to your health system, establish the four tuning knobs of enemy difficulty, and run a rigorous partner playtest.

Comparative Thinking ~10 min

Notice how our earlier lessons directly solve today's challenge:

  • How is a projectile hitting the player similar to a spike? Both reduce the player's life by invoking StatManager.manager.ChangeHealth(-damage).
  • How is a projectile similar to a coin? Both use trigger colliders (Is Trigger = true) and call Destroy(gameObject) upon contact.

Socratic: Where Does the Hit Detection Belong?

  1. Should OnTriggerEnter2D check for hits inside PlayerController.cs or inside Projectile.cs? Why is placing the collision handler on the projectile better when your game introduces arrows, magic blasts, and boss lasers later?
  2. What happens if the projectile accidentally damages other enemies or the turret that spawned it? How does other.CompareTag("Player") ensure safety?
API Documentation & Isolated Patterns ~15 min

Connecting collision physics to gameplay consequences requires three distinct programming operations: filtering target identity, invoking external state managers, and cleaning up spent game objects. Study these isolated function patterns from disparate computing systems:

API MethodSignature / SyntaxEngine Behavior
OnTriggerEnter2D void OnTriggerEnter2D(Collider2D other) Executed automatically when a trigger collider overlaps another collider in 2D space.
CompareTag bool CompareTag(string tag) High-performance string tag check on the colliding object to identify its classification.
Destroy Destroy(Object obj) Schedules a GameObject or Component for removal from memory at the end of the active frame.

Pattern 1: Tag Filtering (Airport Luggage Scanner)

An automated security conveyor inspects baggage tags to route hazardous materials to an isolation bay: 

// Inspects luggage tag metadata before routing
void InspectLuggage(Collider2D item)
{
    if (item.CompareTag("HazardousCargo"))
    {
        RerouteToContainment();
    }
}

Pattern 2: Global Service Invocation (Power Grid Overload)

An industrial transformer discharges a surge into a central energy grid by invoking a singleton manager: 

// Modifies a global energy pool via singleton access
void DischargeToGrid(int wattsToDrain)
{
    if (PowerGridManager.instance != null)
    {
        // Passing a negative number decrements the central pool
        PowerGridManager.instance.AdjustPowerSupply(-wattsToDrain);
    }
}

Pattern 3: Impact Disposal (Firework Rocket Casing)

A spent pyrotechnic shell destroys its own physical casing upon detonation to prevent duplicate impacts: 

// Removes this GameObject immediately from the active scene hierarchy
Destroy(gameObject);

Predict Before Building

  1. If you omit Destroy(gameObject); from an impact callback, what happens if the moving entity remains inside the target collider for 10 consecutive frames?
  2. Notice how DischargeToGrid passes negative -wattsToDrain to AdjustPowerSupply(). What would happen in our game if we mistakenly passed positive damage to ChangeHealth()?
  3. Why is checking if (StatManager.manager != null) critical before attempting to invoke ChangeHealth()?
Build Lab: Your Turn ~25 min
Architectural Specification for Projectile.cs:

Damage Tuning Knob:

  • What serialized integer variable should allow designers to configure how punishing each projectile hit is? What default value makes sense?

Handle Player Hit:

  • What function does this belong in?
  • Should a projectile be a trigger or a collider? (Hint: Does a bullet stop the player like a brick wall, or pass into them to register a hit?)
  • How do you check if the collided object is the Player? Why is this check critical? (What would happen if the projectile collided with the turret that spawned it or an environmental obstacle?)
  • How do you check to see if the StatManager exists before communicating with it?
  • What function on the manager do you call to change health? Should you pass a positive or negative number to inflict damage?
  • How do you destroy the projectile? Is the projectile gameObject or is it other.gameObject? (Hint: this script is attached to the projectile; we collided with other).

Save and test in Unity. Walk into a bullet: your health drops from 3 to 2, the bullet vanishes, and taking 3 hits triggers the death loop and resets to Start!

Step 2 — The Difficulty Matrix. Game difficulty is not arbitrary; it is an equation controlled by four numbers you own:

Knob (Component)DefaultPlayer Experience
maxAttackRange (Turret)7How much of the map is a danger zone
attackCooldown (Turret)2sHow much time the player gets between dodges
speed (Projectile)6How much human reaction time is required
damage (Projectile)1How punishing each mistake is (out of 3 health)

Step 3 — Build Three Turret Personalities. Duplicate the Turret in your Overworld scene (Ctrl+D) to create three distinct challenges:

  • The Sniper: Huge range (12), long cooldown (3.5s), fast bullet (14), high damage (2).
  • The Sentry: Short range (4), rapid cooldown (0.8s), slow bullet (4), low damage (1).
  • The Mortar: Medium range (7), balanced cooldown (2s), huge slow projectile (3), fatal damage (3).

Bug Hunt: The Unfair Encounter

  1. What happens if a turret has speed = 25 and attackCooldown = 0.2s? What is the technical difference between an encounter that is "hard" and one that is "statistically impossible"?
  2. If you place a Sniper turret directly at the scene entrance where the player spawns, why does that violate player trust?
Playtest ~20 min

Swap seats with a partner and run a silent playtest (2.4a rules). Observe their run through your Overworld without speaking:

  • Did they notice the turret before it fired, or was the first hit a surprise?
  • Did they try to dodge bullets, or did they simply sprint through damage?
  • Which of your three turret personalities felt the most satisfying to evade?

Tinker: Close the Loop

  1. From your partner's feedback, pick one single knob to adjust (e.g. decrease projectile speed from 14 to 11). Retest. Did the play experience immediately improve?
  2. Commit and push your work: "3.4a: turret damage, personalities & playtest".

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Implement OnTriggerEnter2D on projectiles to deliver damage to the player
  • Explain how projectile collision reuses the damage and pickup patterns from Unit 2
  • Identify the four parameters that define turret encounter difficulty
  • Tune multiple turret archetypes using serialized Inspector overrides
  • Conduct a partner playtest and make an evidence-based design revision
